messages:
anya: thinking out loud — we should support an automated 'transparent reroute' when a primary model hits sustained capacity pressure. not full eviction, just demote traffic to a compatible variant in the same region/tier. low config surface for users, high observability for us.
kevin: +1 to the idea. question: how do we define "compatible"? same architecture + same tokenizer? or also allow quantized variants?
samir: propose compatibility ruleset: arch match OR verified runtime-compatible (tokenizer + logits-shape). allow quantized variants if quality delta < 2% on golden prompts. use capacity threshold windowed over 30s (p95 > 85%) to trigger demotion.
paula: console/ops asks: expose toggle per-customer (on/off + max-cost-delta). want to see counts: demote_count, demote_rate, median_latency(primary), median_latency(variant). also ability to force-revert.
kevin: routing algo details: avoid cold-swap storms — do gradual probablistic reroute: start at 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 60s if pressure persists. combine with local sticky cookie per-api-key so a short session isn't split too often.
anya: love the gradual percent ramp. also need backpressure signal to callers (429 vs slower latency). prefer transparent reroute over 429s for high-tier customers.
paula: UX for rollout: in console show a timeline and toggles: "demote policy (auto)" with slider for ramp aggressiveness, and "cost cap" which prevents demote if variant is > X% more expensive.
samir: implementation sketch for router header (internal API):
```
X-Redwood-Routing: prefer=primary;fallback=compatible;ramp=5,25,50;sticky=true;ttl=300
```
router can parse and override per-tenant settings.
kevin: telemetry: emit events when demotion starts/updates/stops with tags: tenant_id, primary_model, variant_model, reason=capacity, ramp_step, trigger_metric. example: demote.start
telemetry-bot: sample event JSON (anonymized):
```
{ "evt":"demote.start", "tenant":"t-123", "prim":"rwkv-1b", "var":"rwkv-1b-8bit", "reason":"p95>85%","ramp":5 }
```
ops-bot: FYI we saw a customer incident yesterday where an abrupt failover caused 50% requests to hit cold variant GPUs — that spiked latency. want to ensure warm-up and weighting prevents that.
anya: agree — require variant warm cache hit ratio threshold (kv-cache warming) before increasing ramp. maybe a pre-warm phase: route <1% for 30s then increase.
paula: console should surface "warm status" for each candidate variant and warnings if warm below threshold. also provide a quick action: "pre-warm variant" which schedules a synthetic traffic job.
samir: one more: make demotion idempotent and traceable — add header `X-Redwood-Demotion-ID` and include in traces so we can correlate traces/metrics.
kevin: edge case: tenant pinned to exact model version. policy should respect pin unless tenant opts into auto-demote. default: off for pinned tenants.
anya: ok TODOs: 1) samir + kevin to draft proto for router header + ramp algorithm (PR) 2) telemetry-bot to add demote.* events (schema) 3) paula to mock console controls and warm-status UI 4) ops to run rehearsal job for pre-warm API.
paula: I'll add console mocks to Figma and link in the doc.
anya: thanks — will sync in sync-up tomorrow. :thumbsup:
